post.title: Why printer ink costs so much when printers are cheap
post.ig:
Your printer is cheap on purpose. The ink is the product.

In January 2024, HP's CEO told CNBC that HP loses money on printers and makes it on supplies.
HP's FY2025 10-K: printer hardware $5.8B vs supplies (ink, toner) $10.9B, about 65% of printing revenue (62.8% in FY2021).
In 2019, Which? found branded ink cost about £1.89 per ml, roughly ten times vintage champagne.
Lawsuits alleged HP's Dynamic Security firmware blocked non-HP cartridges; HP settled a US case for $1.5M in 2019 without admitting wrongdoing; a 2025 toner case settled with HP denying wrongdoing. Example: a $60 printer + four $40 refills a year = $480 of ink in 3 years.

Sources: HP 10-K filings (FY2021-FY2025), CNBC via BetaNews/PetaPixel (Jan 2024), Which? via The Drinks Business (2019), court filings, The Register (2025).
News and education, not financial advice.

Printers are sold cheap because the money is in ink: in HP's fiscal 2025 10-K, supplies brought in $10.9 billion versus $5.8 billion for printer hardware, about 65% of printing revenue. In 2019 Which? found branded ink cost about £1.89 per ml, and HP settled a 2019 US lawsuit alleging its Dynamic Security firmware blocked non-HP cartridges for $1.5 million, admitting no wrongdoing. Sources: HP 10-K filings, CNBC (Jan 2024), Which?, court filings. News and education, not financial advice.
